title: SNAP administrative routes can change participation without establishing household security
source_unit: study-specific SNAP applicant, participant, administrative case, census tract, or recertification case
geography: United States; study-specific states and localities

observations.period: Study-specific period; incumbent SNAP participants subject to work requirements

denominator.unit: study-specific incumbent SNAP participants and subject adults in linked SNAP/earnings administrative data; exact count not disclosed in the extraction memo

incumbent_exit_change.unit: percentage points; reported exit increase after 18 months

overall_participation_change.unit: percent overall reduction in program participation among adults subject to the requirement

observations.method: Regression-discontinuity analysis using linked SNAP and earnings administrative data; source is an NBER working paper later published in the American Economic Journal: Economic Policy.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate is requirement- and population-specific. The study does not observe the full household food, debt, health, time, trust, or political path after exit, and any earnings result is not equivalent to household security.
observations.subgroup: Incumbent SNAP participants and adults subject to the work requirement, with a reported homeless-adult subgroup pattern.
observations.counterinterpretation: A change in participation can reflect eligibility enforcement, reporting, or administrative screening rather than a change in work capacity; no employment effect does not by itself prove a food-security effect.

observations.period: Study-specific period; Los Angeles SNAP applicant field experiment

denominator.unit: approximately 65,000 SNAP applicants in the reported field experiment

flexible_interview_approval_change.unit: percentage points; reported change in approvals

longer_term_participation_change.unit: more than percentage points; reported change in longer-term participation

observations.method: Field experiment comparing applicant-initiated flexible interviews with the study comparison route; source is an NBER working paper.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates belong to the Los Angeles setting, study period, applicant pool, treatment implementation, and outcome definitions; later food, debt, health, trust, and political outcomes are not observed in this record.
observations.subgroup: SNAP applicants in the Los Angeles study setting, differentiated by interview route.
observations.counterinterpretation: Approval and continued participation can change because of selection, information, or timing without proving improved household security or a universal effect of flexible interviews.

observations.period: Study-specific two-year post-event window; one-state SNAP office openings and closings

denominator.unit: study-specific SNAP administrative cases linked to geocoded offices and census tracts; exact count not disclosed in the extraction memo

office_closure_participation_change.unit: percent decline in tract SNAP participation over two years after office closure

observations.method: Administrative SNAP cases linked to geocoded offices using event-study variation; source is an NBER working paper.
observations.uncertainty: The result is from one state and a place-based participation outcome; opening effects are described as suggestive and the study does not measure food security or same-person interpretation.
observations.subgroup: SNAP participants and census tracts differentiated by office exposure, with urban concentration noted for opening effects.
observations.counterinterpretation: Office closures may coincide with local need, migration, or service changes; participation is not the same as take-up among all eligible households or household security.

observations.period: Study-specific policy period; parents exposed to general SNAP work requirements

denominator.unit: study-specific parents in linked administrative records; exact count not disclosed in the extraction memo

employment_response.unit: reported employment outcome in the study setting

observations.method: Linked administrative-record analysis of parents exposed to general SNAP work requirements; source is an NBER working paper.
observations.uncertainty: The result is policy- and state-specific and does not estimate every work-requirement design or downstream household food, debt, health, time, trust, or political outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Parents in the study population exposed to the general work requirement.
observations.counterinterpretation: Employment measurement, implementation, exemptions, alternative support, and local labor-market conditions may alter the observed response; lower receipt is not itself proof of harm or improved independence.

observations.period: Study-specific recent policy period; age-based exemption design

denominator.unit: study-specific administrative SNAP records around an age-based exemption threshold; exact count not disclosed in the extraction memo

procedural_denial_response.unit: reported procedural and overall denial response under work requirements

observations.method: Difference-in-differences around an age-based exemption using administrative data; source is a recent NBER working paper.
observations.uncertainty: This is a design-specific result and is not a national denial rate; the source is labeled a working paper and downstream household outcomes are not observed.
observations.subgroup: Administrative cases near the study's age-based exemption threshold.
observations.counterinterpretation: Threshold-specific behavior, composition, implementation, or other age-correlated changes may affect the estimate; procedural denial is not identical to ineligibility or durable exit.

observations.period: Study-specific recertification episodes; NBER Reporter 2024 discussion

denominator.unit: study-specific administrative recertification cases; exact count not disclosed in the extraction memo

recertification_failure.unit: reported share of cases failing recertification

below_threshold_among_rejected.unit: reported qualitative share of rejected cases appearing below the earnings threshold

near_term_reentry.unit: reported share of failures reentering soon after

observations.method: Administrative recertification-case analysis discussed in the NBER Reporter; timing and route are interpreted as possible administrative churn mechanisms.
observations.uncertainty: The evidence comes from defined administrative settings and does not measure every reason for failure, full household security, or political meaning.
observations.subgroup: SNAP recertification cases differentiated by recertification outcome and subsequent reentry.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reentry can reflect changing need, corrected records, ordinary eligibility changes, or other unobserved routes; failure and reentry should not be treated as a single causal churn estimate without the underlying case definitions.

related_sources.claim: USDA ERS summarizes SNAP food-security, poverty, participation, and economic-linkage research; these outcomes remain distinct from administrative participation routes.
The companion SIPP record provides national person-month transition and following-hardship context with Fay-BRR uncertainty.

boundary: This record preserves study-specific causal or reported participation/denial mechanisms from NBER-linked administrative and field studies and places them beside, but does not pool them with, the national SIPP transition-to-hardship record. It does not estimate one national administrative-burden effect, same-household food or health consequences, benefit adequacy, trust, political action, or a program effect across designs. The committed paper-scan hash covers the source-specific extraction memo.
